name.security_impact: If naming is not controlled, deny policies become hard to identify and manage, which can cause security confusion.
name.rationale: We enforce a simple naming rule using prefix 'pde-' so all deny policies are consistent and easy to track.

parent.description: The attachment point is identified by its URL-encoded full resource name.
parent.security_impact: If parent is wrong, deny policy may be applied to the wrong project or not applied at all, which is a major security risk.
parent.rationale: Parent must always follow valid GCP resource format so the deny policy is applied to the correct scope.

rules.security_impact: Rules define what access is denied. Incorrect rules can either block valid users or allow unauthorized access.
rules.rationale: Rules are used to enforce strict deny controls on sensitive resources.

display_name.description: The display name of the rule.
display_name.security_impact: Helps identify the deny policy in console and audit logs.
display_name.rationale: Used for readability and easier management of policies.

deny_rule.security_impact: Controls which users and permissions are explicitly blocked from accessing resources.
deny_rule.rationale: Used to enforce security restrictions and prevent unauthorized actions.

denied_principals.description: Users or identities that are blocked from access.
denied_principals.security_impact: Prevents unauthorized users from accessing sensitive resources.
denied_principals.rationale: We block risky or unwanted identities using deny rules.

denied_permissions.security_impact: Prevents execution of sensitive or admin-level operations.
denied_permissions.rationale: We deny high-risk permissions to enforce least privilege.

denial_condition.description: Condition when the deny rule should apply.
denial_condition.security_impact: Adds conditional security checks (like time, IP, or context-based restrictions).
denial_condition.rationale: Used to apply deny rules only in specific situations.
